name: Vyāsa

realization_account.text: Son of Parāśara and Satyavatī, a portion of Viṣṇu (BhP 1.3.21: the seventeenth avatāra), who divided the Veda and, in every Dvāpara age, condenses the one primeval Purāṇa into eighteen (Matsya 53.8-11); dissatisfied after composing the Mahābhārata, he was told by Nārada to describe the Lord's glories, and in trance composed the Bhāgavata (BhP 1.5-7).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: In the Purāṇic tradition the compiler of the eighteen Purāṇas (and Upapurāṇas through his disciples, KūP 1.1.280), who gave the Purāṇa-saṃhitā to his sūta disciple Romaharṣaṇa (VP 3.6.15-16) and the Bhāgavata to his son Śuka.

name: Romaharṣaṇa

realization_account.text: The sūta disciple to whom Vyāsa gave the Purāṇa-saṃhitā; his own saṃhitā is the root (mūla) of the three made by his disciples (VP 3.6.16-18). BhP 12.7.5-7 names six paurāṇikas who learned from him.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The first paurāṇika: Vyāsa's disciple for the Purāṇa, reciter at Naimiṣa in several Purāṇas, father of Ugraśravas; the four root saṃhitās of the Purāṇa descend from him and his pupils.

name: Ugraśravas
summary: Son of Romaharṣaṇa, the Sūta who recites the Bhāgavata and other Purāṇas to Śaunaka and the sages of the Naimiṣa forest (having heard the Bhāgavata from Śuka at Parīkṣit's assembly); he learned all four root saṃhitās (BhP 12.7.6).

name: Akṛtavraṇa
summary: One of Romaharṣaṇa's disciples in both lists (VP 3.6.17; BhP 12.7.5), of the Kāśyapa lineage (VP 3.6.18 counts 'Kāśyapa' among the makers of saṃhitās; BhP 12.7.7 calls Akṛtavraṇa a disciple of Rāma Jāmadagnya).

name: Sāvarṇi (paurāṇika)
summary: Disciple of Romaharṣaṇa and maker of one of the root Purāṇa-saṃhitās (VP 3.6.17-18; BhP 12.7.5-7). Not to be confused with the Manu Sāvarṇi (the eighth Manu).

name: Śāṃśapāyana
summary: Disciple of Romaharṣaṇa and maker of one of the root Purāṇa-saṃhitās (VP 3.6.17-18); absent from the Bhāgavata's list of six paurāṇikas, which names Trayyāruṇi, Kaśyapa, Sāvarṇi, Akṛtavraṇa, Vaiśampāyana and Hārīta instead (BhP 12.7.5).

name: Śuka

realization_account.text: Born liberated and absorbed in Brahman, he was drawn by the qualities of Hari to learn the Bhāgavata from his father (BhP 1.7.9-11); an avadhūta wandering naked whom women did not notice as a man (BhP 1.4.5); he recited the Bhāgavata to Parīkṣit in seven days and ended with the non-dual instruction 'I am Brahman, the supreme abode' (BhP 12.5.11).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Vyāsa's son, the paramahaṃsa narrator of the Bhāgavata to King Parīkṣit on the bank of the Gaṅgā; one of the twelve 'great ones' (mahājana) who know the dharma of devotion (BhP 6.3.20, 'vaiyāsaki').

name: Parīkṣit
summary: Grandson of Arjuna, protected in the womb by Kṛṣṇa; cursed to die in seven days, he renounced his kingdom and sat in prāyopaveśa on the Gaṅgā (BhP 1.19), where he heard the Bhāgavata from Śuka; the model hearer (śravaṇa) of the Purāṇa. He also subdued Kali and assigned him five places (BhP 1.17).

name: Śaunaka (of Naimiṣa)
summary: The kulapati of the thousand-year sacrificial session (sattra) at the Naimiṣa forest who questions the Sūta in the frame of the Bhāgavata and other Purāṇas. Tradition's link to the Vedic Śaunakas is not asserted here.

name: Parāśara
summary: Grandson of Vasiṣṭha and father of Vyāsa; the speaker of the Viṣṇu Purāṇa to Maitreya, which he received from Vasiṣṭha and Pulastya after renouncing his rite to burn the rākṣasas (VP 1.1.12-26).

name: Maitreya (sage)
summary: The sage who questions Parāśara in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (VP 1.1.1-11) and who, in the Bhāgavata's third and fourth books, instructs Vidura on creation and the Lord's deeds. Not the Buddhist Maitreya.

name: Nārada

realization_account.text: In a former life the son of a maidservant who served Vedāntin sages, heard Hari's glories, had a vision of the Lord and was told he would see him again only in a later body (BhP 1.5.23-1.6.38); reborn as the celestial sage who wanders singing Hari's names with his vīṇā. BhP 1.3.8 counts him the third avatāra, who 'expounded the Sātvata tantra'.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The divine sage and wandering devotee: teacher of Vyāsa (urging him to write the Bhāgavata), initiator of Dhruva with the twelve-syllable mantra, teacher of Prahlāda while still in his mother's womb, pupil of the Kumāras in the Nārada Purāṇa; one of the twelve mahājanas (BhP 6.3.20).

name: Prahlāda

realization_account.text: Son of the demon-king Hiraṇyakaśipu, devoted to Viṣṇu from the womb; unharmed by his father's attempts to kill him; saved by Narasiṃha; refuses boons and liberation for himself alone (BhP 7.4-10; VP 1.16-20).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The child-devotee who taught his demon schoolfellows the nine forms of devotion (BhP 7.5.23-24) and that devotion should be practised from childhood (7.6.1); a mahājana (6.3.20) and king of the daityas in Sutala.

name: Dhruva
summary: Son of King Uttānapāda; slighted by his stepmother, he went to the forest as a child, was initiated by Nārada (BhP 4.8) - or taught by the seven sages (VP 1.11-12) - and by austere meditation on Vāsudeva won the vision of Viṣṇu and the eternal position of the pole-star (dhruva-sthāna).

name: Jaḍa Bharata

realization_account.text: The king after whom Bhāratavarṣa is named retired to the forest, became attached to an orphaned fawn, died thinking of it and was reborn as a deer; then reborn as a brahmin who, remembering, lived as if dull and dumb, and taught the king of Sindhu-Sauvīra (Rahūgaṇa) the distinction of self and body (BhP 5.7-14; VP 2.13-16).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The exemplar of the power of the last thought (anta-smṛti) and of the avadhūta who hides his realization; teacher of Rahūgaṇa.

name: Rahūgaṇa
summary: The king who forced Jaḍa Bharata to carry his palanquin and received from him instruction on the self beyond the body (BhP 5.10-13; the VP 2.13-16 version names the king of Sauvīra).

name: Ṛṣabha

realization_account.text: Son of Nābhi and Merudevī, the eighth avatāra 'who showed the path honoured by all āśramas' (BhP 1.3.13); after teaching his sons that the human body is not for dog-like pleasures but for austerity (BhP 5.5.1-27), he lived as a naked avadhūta and gave up his body in a forest fire in Kuṭaka (BhP 5.5.28-5.6.8).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: In the Bhāgavata an avatāra of Viṣṇu and avadhūta-teacher; the same figure the Jains honour as the first Tīrthaṅkara. BhP 5.6.9 adds that a king named Arhat of Koṅka, Veṅka and Kuṭaka, imitating him, will spread a heterodox path in Kali (a polemical report).

name: Kapila

realization_account.text: Son of Kardama and Devahūti, the fifth avatāra who taught Sāṃkhya to Āsuri (BhP 1.3.10) and instructed his mother in devotion and yoga (BhP 3.25-33, the Kapila Gītā owned by U06).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: In the Bhāgavata the avatāra-teacher of Sāṃkhya, eight-limbed yoga directed to the Lord's form (BhP 3.28) and devotion; a mahājana (6.3.20).

name: Devahūti
summary: Daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu, wife of Kardama and mother of Kapila, who asked her son for the path to liberation, received the Kapila Gītā and attained perfection through its yoga (BhP 3.25-33).

name: Dattātreya

realization_account.text: Son of Atri and Anasūyā (a portion of Viṣṇu; in some accounts of the Trimūrti), the sixth avatāra who 'taught ānvīkṣikī to Alarka, Prahlāda and others' (BhP 1.3.11); an avadhūta who hid his yoga under outward impurity (MkP 16-19); in the Bhāgavata he tells of his twenty-four teachers (BhP 11.7-9, U06).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The avadhūta yogin of the Purāṇas whose teaching to Alarka (MkP 37-43) is the Mārkaṇḍeya's yoga: discrimination of self and body, posture, breath, dhāraṇā, obstacles, powers, Oṃ and the signs of death.

name: Alarka
summary: Youngest son of Madālasā and King Ṛtadhvaja (Kuvalayāśva); raised as a king, he received his mother's ring-instruction and, when defeated in war, went to Dattātreya, learned yoga and renounced (MkP 25-44).

name: Madālasā

realization_account.text: The queen who, under pretext of lulling her crying infants, taught her first sons that the self is pure, that its name is a recent imagination, and that the body of five elements is not theirs (MkP 25.10-18), so that they renounced; she taught Alarka rājadharma and gave him a ring containing a teaching for the time of distress (MkP 26-35).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: A woman teacher of self-knowledge in the Mārkaṇḍeya. Her lullaby opens 'śuddho 'si re tāta, na te 'sti nāma' in the checked e-text (MkP 25.11); the popular verse 'śuddho 'si buddho 'si nirañjano 'si ...' recited under her name was not found there.

name: Sumati ('Jaḍa')
summary: Son of a Bhārgava brahmin who behaved like a dullard (jaḍa) because he remembered past births; he told his father how beings are born, die, travel to Yama and suffer in hell (MkP 10-15), the account the wise birds relate to Jaimini.

name: Mārkaṇḍeya

realization_account.text: The long-lived sage who, by Nara-Nārāyaṇa's boon, witnessed an illusory deluge and saw the Lord as an infant lying on a banyan leaf, entering and leaving the child's body (BhP 12.8-10).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The ever-young sage in whose name the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is told; he directs Jaimini to the wise birds and narrates the Devī Māhātmya as the story of the eighth Manu.

name: Jaimini
summary: In the Purāṇas Vyāsa's disciple for the Sāmaveda (VP 3.4), and the questioner of the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, who asks about the Mahābhārata's puzzles and then about birth, death and liberation. (His identity with the Mīmāṃsā-sūtra author is the traditional view.)

name: Medhas
summary: The brahmin sage (dvijavarya, MkP 81.9) in whose forest hermitage the Devī Māhātmya is taught to the deposed king Suratha and the merchant Samādhi.

name: Suratha
summary: A king of the Caitra line, deposed by enemies and ministers; after hearing the Devī Māhātmya he worshipped the Goddess for three years and received his kingdom back and the boon of becoming Sāvarṇi, the eighth Manu (DM 13; MkP 93.17).

name: Samādhi (the merchant)
summary: A merchant cast out by his greedy family who still could not stop worrying about them; with Suratha he heard the Devī Māhātmya, and asked the Goddess not for wealth but for the knowledge that frees from attachment, which she granted (DM 13).

name: Hayagrīva
summary: The horse-headed form of Viṣṇu (BhP 2.7.11), who in the Lalitopākhyāna is sent as a portion of Viṣṇu to teach Agastya the story and worship of Lalitā.

name: Agastya
summary: In the Purāṇas the sage who, pilgrimaging with Lopāmudrā, receives the Lalitopākhyāna from Hayagrīva, and who in the Kāśī Khaṇḍa teaches Lopāmudrā the inner tīrthas (SkP 4.1.6.28-45); he also cursed Indradyumna to become the elephant Gajendra.

name: Lopāmudrā
summary: Agastya's wife and companion in pilgrimage in the Kāśī Khaṇḍa, questioner on tīrthas; in the Śrīvidyā tradition a seer of a form of the Goddess's mantra (U23).

name: Garuḍa
summary: The eagle-mount of Viṣṇu to whom Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa teaches the Garuḍa Purāṇa; his questions in the Pretakalpa frame the teaching on death and the dead.

name: Upamanyu
summary: The Śaiva sage who, having won Śiva's favour as a child through austerity, gives Kṛṣṇa Pāśupata initiation and teaches him Śaiva doctrine, worship, the pañcākṣara and yoga in the Vāyavīya Saṃhitā (ŚiP 7.2) and in LiP 1.107.

name: Sanatkumāra
summary: Eldest of the four Kumāras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, Sanatkumāra), mind-born sons of Brahmā who refused to procreate and remained celibate knowers (VP 1.7; KūP 1.10.13-14); the first avatāra in BhP 1.3.6; with his brothers he instructs Nārada in the Nārada Purāṇa; the first Upapurāṇa bears his name (KūP 1.1.17).

name: Keśidhvaja
summary: A Janaka king devoted to knowledge (ātma-vidyā) who, though acting through karma to exhaust it, taught his rival kinsman Khāṇḍikya the nature of ignorance and the eightfold yoga with Viṣṇu as support (VP 6.6-7); he attained liberation by acting without attachment (VP 6.7.105-106).

name: Khāṇḍikya Janaka
summary: A Janaka king devoted to ritual action (karma), expelled by Keśidhvaja; asked by him for the expiation for a killed cow, he chose instead to ask for the teaching of yoga, then renounced and dissolved into the Brahman called Viṣṇu (VP 6.6-7.104).

name: Ṛbhu
summary: Mind-born son of Brahmā (KūP 1.10.13 lists him with the Kumāras) who teaches his disciple Nidāgha the non-difference of all selves (VP 2.15-16) - told within Jaḍa Bharata's teaching; the Ṛbhu Gītā (U06) is a separate text.

name: Nidāgha
summary: Pulastya's son and Ṛbhu's disciple, visited by his teacher twice in disguise and brought to see that there is no difference between 'king' and 'elephant', 'I' and 'you' (VP 2.15-16).

name: Uddhava
summary: Kṛṣṇa's friend and counsellor, sent to Vraja with Kṛṣṇa's message to the gopīs, whose love in separation he came to revere (BhP 10.46-47); later the recipient of the Uddhava Gītā (BhP 11.7-29, owned by U06).

name: Śrīdhara Svāmin
summary: The most influential commentator on the Bhāgavata and the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (and on the Gītā, Subodhinī), a renunciant whose non-dualism is devotional (Narasiṃha-bhakti); later Vaiṣṇava schools build on or argue with his readings.

name: Viṣṇucitta
summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava author of the Viṣṇucittīya commentary on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (dating not checked in this sweep).

name: Bhāskararāya
summary: In this unit: author of the Guptavatī commentary on the Devī Māhātmya (his Śrīvidyā works belong to U23).

name: Vopadeva
summary: Grammarian (Mugdhabodha) who wrote works on the Bhāgavata (the Muktāphala and the Harilīlāmṛta, the latter a summary of its contents); opponents of the Bhāgavata's status later claimed he composed the Bhāgavata itself, a claim its defenders reject (dsp:which-bhagavata-is-the-mahapurana).

name: Lakṣmīdhara

scholarly.text: 12th c. CE, minister of the Gāhaḍavāla king Govindacandra

summary: Author of the Kṛtyakalpataru, the digest that systematised Purāṇic teaching on vows, gifts, tīrthas and śrāddha.

name: Hemādri

scholarly.text: 13th c. CE, minister at the Yādava court

summary: Author of the Caturvargacintāmaṇi, whose volumes on vows and gifts are the fullest compilation of Purāṇic vrata and dāna.
